biggest_catch: Aspire is an enterprise influencer platform for mid-to-large brands: its official materials state that pay is negotiated per brief between brand and creator ('It is up to you to negotiate payment with the creator') — no rate, range, or minimum exists on its official domain.
catches: Aspire's official help center explicitly says creator payment is negotiated per brief — there is no platform rate card.
The '$250M+ paid out to creators' figure is an aggregate platform claim, not a per-creator pay term.
Aspire is positioned for mid-sized to large e-commerce brands with enterprise-level pricing — campaign flow favors established creators, not beginners.
No creator minimum pay, per-post rate, or payout timeline is published on official pages.

c1.evidence: No concrete creator pay figure (no per-post rate, range, or minimum) found on any official Aspire page (aspire.io, creators.aspireiq.com, help.aspireiq.com).

c2.evidence: aspire.io / creators.aspireiq.com are the official domains; official pages describe the marketplace without creator pay figures.

c3.evidence: No upfront creator fee stated; enterprise pricing is brand-side.

c4.evidence: No creator payout timing published on official pages.

eligibility: Not stated as creator pay terms — the Creator Marketplace lets brands post campaigns and creators apply; terms are per-brief.
notes: REJECT is a verifiability verdict, not a scam flag: Aspire (formerly AspireIQ) is a real, large influencer platform (150,000+ active creators, $250M+ paid out per its site), but the strict checklist requires a concrete payout in official terms and none exists — pay is explicitly per-brief negotiation. Do not list this route as verified. Re-check if Aspire publishes creator rate guidance.

s1.note: No public creator eligibility or pay terms; per-brief negotiation.

s2.note: Pay negotiated per brief; no minimums; brand-selection risk total.

s4.note: '$250M+ paid out to creators' aggregate claim implies earning ease without any per-creator figure.
